Real-World Impact: Psychologists help students deal with exam stress, help people recover from anxiety or depression, and help companies like Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) or Infosys design better workplaces. Schools like those in the Delhi government system now have counsellors to support students' mental health.
Entry Exams: No single fixed entrance exam for a bachelor's degree — most colleges admit based on Class 12 marks, though some like Delhi University use CUET (Common University Entrance Test, a single exam many central universities use for admission). For a master's degree, exams like CUET-PG or university-specific tests are common.
Top Colleges: University of Delhi, Tata Institute of Social Sciences (TISS) Mumbai, Christ University Bangalore, Fergusson College Pune, NIMHANS Bangalore, Ashoka University
Top Recruiters: Hospitals and mental health clinics, schools and colleges, corporate HR departments (TCS, Infosys, Wipro), NGOs like Sangath, private counselling practices
Where You Can Work: Works from anywhere (many now offer online therapy)
Notable People: Dr. Achal Bhagat (psychiatrist and mental health advocate), Kamlesh Singh (professor, IIT Delhi psychology), Dr. Anna Chandy (India's first female psychotherapist)
Sources: NIRF rankings, AmbitionBox, Glassdoor India, industry placement reports
Common Specializations (Optional): Clinical Psychology: Diagnoses and treats mental health issues like depression or anxiety, often in hospitals or clinics. | Counseling Psychology: Helps people work through everyday life problems like relationships, stress, or career confusion. | Organizational/HR Psychology: Studies how people behave at work and helps companies improve hiring, teamwork, and employee wellbeing.

A Day in the Life: A radiology technologist operates machines like X-ray, CT scan, or MRI machines to take pictures of the inside of a patient's body, following a doctor's instructions. They position patients correctly, run the machine safely, and hand over the images to doctors who then read and diagnose from them.
Real-World Impact: When someone breaks a bone or a doctor needs to check for a tumour, it's the radiology technologist who actually operates the machine that captures the image, at hospitals like Apollo, Fortis, or AIIMS. Without them, doctors would have no way to see what's happening inside a patient's body.
Entry Exams: No single fixed entrance exam — most students join a diploma or B.Sc. in Radiography/Medical Imaging Technology after Class 12 (with Physics, Chemistry, Biology) based on marks or a college-specific entrance test. Note: this is different from becoming a radiologist doctor, which needs MBBS plus a specialization (covered separately under Medicine).
Top Colleges: AIIMS New Delhi, Christian Medical College (CMC) Vellore, Manipal College of Health Professions, Kasturba Medical College, Jawaharlal Institute of Postgraduate Medical Education and Research (JIPMER), Tata Memorial Centre School of Radiography
Top Recruiters: Apollo Hospitals, Fortis Healthcare, Max Healthcare, AIIMS, diagnostic chains like Dr Lal PathLabs and SRL Diagnostics
Notable People: Dr. Bhavin Jankharia (well-known radiologist and imaging expert), technologist training pioneers at AIIMS radiology departments
Sources: NIRF rankings, AmbitionBox, Glassdoor India, industry placement reports

A Day in the Life: A robotics engineer designs, builds, and programs robots or automated machines, writing code to control motors and sensors and testing the robot physically to see if it moves and reacts the way it should.
Real-World Impact: The robotic arms that assemble cars at Mahindra and Maruti Suzuki factories, and drone systems used for farming and delivery in India, are built and programmed by robotics engineers.
Entry Exams: JEE Main and JEE Advanced (national engineering entrance exams), or state entrance exams, for a BTech in Robotics Engineering or Mechatronics; some students enter via a Mechanical, Electronics, or Computer Science BTech first.
Top Colleges: IIT Kanpur, IIT Bombay, IIIT Hyderabad, VIT Vellore, Manipal Institute of Technology, IIT Kharagpur
Top Recruiters: Tata Elxsi, Bosch, Siemens, Mahindra Robotics, ABB India, GreyOrange
Notable People: Vijay Kumar: Indian-origin robotics professor and dean at University of Pennsylvania | Ashutosh Saxena: founder of Caspar AI, robotics and AI researcher
Sources: NIRF rankings, AmbitionBox, Glassdoor India, industry placement reports
Common Specializations (Optional): Industrial Robotics: builds robots used in factories for assembly and welding | Autonomous Systems: works on self-driving vehicles and drones that operate without a human controller | Medical Robotics: designs robots used in surgery and healthcare

A Day in the Life: A safety engineer inspects factories, construction sites, or oil plants to spot hazards, then designs rules and equipment to prevent accidents, fires, or chemical leaks, often walking through work sites wearing safety gear.
Real-World Impact: After major industrial accidents like the Bhopal gas tragedy, safety engineers are the reason companies like Reliance and L&T now have strict systems to prevent chemical leaks, fires, and worker injuries at their plants.
Entry Exams: No single fixed entrance exam for a first degree — safety engineering is usually studied as a postgraduate diploma or master's after a BTech in any engineering branch, with admission based on the earlier degree and sometimes GATE (a national postgraduate entrance exam) scores.
Top Colleges: National Institute of Occupational Health, Central Labour Institute Mumbai, Andhra University, Anna University, PSG College of Technology, Regional Labour Institute
Top Recruiters: Reliance Industries, L&T, ONGC, Tata Steel, NTPC (National Thermal Power Corporation), Adani Group
Notable People: J.S. Rao: known figure in Indian industrial safety consulting | R.K. Dixit: veteran safety engineering practitioner in petrochemical plants
Sources: NIRF rankings, AmbitionBox, Glassdoor India, industry placement reports
Common Specializations (Optional): Fire and Process Safety: focuses on preventing fires and chemical accidents in factories | Occupational Health and Safety: focuses on protecting workers' health and preventing workplace injuries | Construction Safety: focuses on hazards specific to building and infrastructure sites

A Day in the Life: A sericulture professional works with farmers to raise silkworms, manage mulberry or other host plant farms, and oversee the process of turning silkworm cocoons into raw silk thread. On a typical day, they might inspect silkworm-rearing houses, check plant health, or guide farmers on disease prevention.
Real-World Impact: India is the world's second-largest silk producer, and sericulture experts help silk farmers in states like Karnataka and West Bengal earn a steady income while supplying silk for sarees and textiles sold by brands like Nalli Silks and Fabindia. Their work supports millions of rural livelihoods tied to the silk industry.
Entry Exams: No single fixed entrance exam — students usually join a B.Sc. in Sericulture after Class 12 (Science stream) based on marks, though some agricultural universities use exams like ICAR AIEEA (a national entrance test for agriculture-related degrees).
Top Colleges: University of Agricultural Sciences Bangalore, Central Sericultural Research and Training Institute (CSRTI) Mysore, Bangalore University, Tamil Nadu Agricultural University, Berhampore Sericulture College
Top Recruiters: Central Silk Board, state departments of sericulture, Karnataka State Sericulture Development Institute, silk trading companies, NGOs supporting rural livelihoods
Where You Can Work: Tier-2 cities fine (mainly rural and semi-rural areas)
Notable People: Scientists at the Central Silk Board, researchers at CSRTI Mysore who developed improved silkworm breeds
Sources: NIRF rankings, AmbitionBox, Glassdoor India, industry placement reports

A Day in the Life: A social worker spends the day meeting with individuals, families, or communities facing difficulties like poverty, abuse, or addiction, and connects them to the help they need, such as government schemes, counselling, or shelters. They might visit slums, run awareness camps, or coordinate with NGOs and government offices.
Real-World Impact: Social workers run programs that help rescue child labourers, support survivors of domestic violence, and help rural families access schemes like the Public Distribution System (PDS) for subsidized food. Organizations like Save the Children and CRY (Child Rights and You) rely on social workers to reach people who need help the most.
Entry Exams: No single fixed entrance exam for a bachelor's degree — admission is usually based on Class 12 marks. For a Master's in Social Work (MSW), exams like TISS-NET (Tata Institute of Social Sciences' own entrance test) or CUET-PG are commonly used.
Top Colleges: Tata Institute of Social Sciences (TISS) Mumbai, Delhi University, Christ University Bangalore, Loyola College Chennai, Jamia Millia Islamia, Nirmala Niketan Mumbai
Top Recruiters: UNICEF, Save the Children, CRY, government welfare departments, hospitals (medical social work), corporate CSR (Corporate Social Responsibility) teams
Notable People: Aruna Roy (social activist, Right to Information movement), Bezwada Wilson (Safai Karamchari Andolan founder), Harsh Mander (social worker and author)
Sources: NIRF rankings, AmbitionBox, Glassdoor India, industry placement reports
Common Specializations (Optional): Medical Social Work: Helps patients and families in hospitals cope with illness, cost of treatment, and access to care. | Community Development: Works directly with villages or urban slums to improve education, health, and livelihoods. | Child and Family Welfare: Focuses on protecting children's rights, adoption processes, and family counselling.

A Day in the Life: A space engineer designs and tests parts of satellites or rockets, like the systems that let a satellite communicate or the engines that launch a rocket into orbit, working through detailed calculations and running tests to make sure everything survives the extreme conditions of space.
Real-World Impact: The Chandrayaan Moon missions and the satellites that give India its GPS-like navigation system and weather forecasts exist because space engineers at ISRO design the rockets and satellites that make it all work.
Entry Exams: JEE Main and JEE Advanced (national engineering entrance exams) for a BTech in Aerospace or Space Engineering, with further entry into ISRO often through IIST admissions or ISRO's own recruitment exam called ICRB.
Top Colleges: Indian Institute of Space Science and Technology (IIST), IIT Bombay, IIT Kharagpur, IIT Kanpur, IISc Bangalore, Manipal Institute of Technology
Top Recruiters: ISRO (Indian Space Research Organisation), Skyroot Aerospace, Agnikul Cosmos, Hindustan Aeronautics Limited, Bharat Dynamics, Antrix Corporation
Notable People: S. Somanath: Chairman of ISRO, led Chandrayaan-3 mission | K. Sivan: former ISRO Chairman during Chandrayaan-2
Sources: NIRF rankings, AmbitionBox, Glassdoor India, industry placement reports
Common Specializations (Optional): Satellite Systems Engineering: designs the equipment inside satellites that lets them orbit and communicate | Launch Vehicle Engineering: designs the rockets that carry satellites into space | Propulsion Engineering: designs the engines and fuel systems that power rockets

A Day in the Life: A structural engineer figures out how strong a building, bridge, or flyover needs to be so it does not fall down, by doing calculations and checking drawings with architects and site teams. They also visit construction sites to check if steel and concrete are being used the way the design says.
Real-World Impact: The people who made sure the Bandra-Worli Sea Link in Mumbai or the Delhi Metro bridges can carry traffic safely without collapsing are structural engineers. Every tall building you see in cities like Bengaluru or Hyderabad needed one to check it will not crack or tip over.
Entry Exams: JEE Main and JEE Advanced (national engineering entrance exams to get into top government colleges) for a Civil Engineering degree with a later specialization in structures, or state-level engineering entrance exams like MHT-CET or KCET for other colleges.
Top Colleges: IIT Delhi, IIT Bombay, IIT Madras, IIT Roorkee, NIT Trichy, VNIT Nagpur
Top Recruiters: L&T Construction, Tata Projects, DLF, AECOM, Shapoorji Pallonji, Jacobs Engineering
Notable People: E. Sreedharan (built Delhi Metro), Fazlur Rahman Khan (designed Burj Khalifa's structure)
Sources: NIRF rankings, AmbitionBox, Glassdoor India, industry placement reports
Common Specializations (Optional): Bridge Engineering: Designing bridges and flyovers that can safely carry vehicles and withstand weather and earthquakes. | Earthquake-Resistant Design: Making buildings strong enough to survive shaking during earthquakes. | High-Rise Building Design: Working out how very tall buildings stay stable against wind and their own weight.

A Day in the Life: A systems engineer looks at the big picture of a complex project, like an aircraft, a satellite, or a company's entire IT network, and makes sure all the different parts (hardware, software, and people) work together smoothly. On a typical day, they might review how a new component will fit into an existing system, spot risks before they become problems, or coordinate between different engineering teams.
Real-World Impact: Systems engineers at the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) make sure that thousands of components in a rocket like Chandrayaan work together perfectly, and at companies like Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) they ensure banks' entire IT systems run without crashing. Their work prevents costly failures in huge, complicated projects.
Entry Exams: JEE Main and JEE Advanced (Joint Entrance Examination, national exams to get into engineering colleges like the IITs) for a bachelor's degree, usually in a core engineering branch first; GATE (Graduate Aptitude Test in Engineering, a national exam for master's programs and government engineering jobs) for further specialization in systems engineering.
Top Colleges: Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Bombay, IIT Madras, Indian Institute of Science (IISc) Bangalore, Birla Institute of Technology and Science (BITS) Pilani, Indian Institute of Space Science and Technology (IIST)
Top Recruiters: Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO), Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO), Tata Consultancy Services (TCS), Boeing India, Larsen & Toubro (L&T)
Notable People: K. Sivan (former ISRO chairman), Ritu Karidhal (ISRO systems engineer, 'Rocket Woman of India'), Nambi Narayanan (ISRO propulsion systems expert)
Sources: NIRF rankings, AmbitionBox, Glassdoor India, industry placement reports

A Day in the Life: A teacher plans lessons, explains topics to students in a classroom, checks homework, and helps students who are struggling to understand a subject. Outside class, they grade tests, prepare study materials, and sometimes meet parents to talk about a student's progress.
Real-World Impact: Teachers shape the futures of millions of students in schools across India, from government schools under the Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan program to private chains like Delhi Public School (DPS), and their teaching often decides whether a child later cracks exams like JEE or simply loves learning. A good teacher can change the direction of a student's entire life.
Entry Exams: No single fixed entrance exam for teaching itself — most people complete a Bachelor's degree followed by a B.Ed. (Bachelor of Education, a professional teaching qualification) which some colleges admit into via marks or state-level tests. To teach in government schools, exams like CTET (Central Teacher Eligibility Test, required to become a government school teacher) are needed.
Top Colleges: Regional Institutes of Education (under NCERT), Delhi University, Jamia Millia Islamia, Tata Institute of Social Sciences (TISS), Azim Premji University
Top Recruiters: Government schools (state education departments), Delhi Public School (DPS) group, Kendriya Vidyalaya Sangathan, Byju's and other ed-tech companies, international schools
Notable People: Sarojini Naidu (poet and educator), Anand Kumar (founder of Super 30, famous math teacher), Kiran Bir Sethi (founder of Riverside School, education innovator)
Sources: NIRF rankings, AmbitionBox, Glassdoor India, industry placement reports
Common Specializations (Optional): Primary School Teaching: Teaches young children (ages 5-11) basic subjects and foundational skills. | Secondary/Subject Teaching: Specializes in one subject like Math or Science for older students (classes 9-12). | Special Education: Works with children who have learning disabilities or other special needs, using customized teaching methods.

A Day in the Life: A textile engineer works on the machines and processes that turn raw fibres like cotton into yarn and then fabric, checking quality and improving how clothes and other fabric products are made in mills and factories.
Real-World Impact: The cotton shirts and sarees sold by brands like Raymond and Arvind Mills, and the denim used in jeans across India, are produced using processes that textile engineers design and manage in mills.
Entry Exams: JEE Main or state engineering entrance exams for a BTech in Textile Engineering or Technology; some institutes like NIFT hold their own entrance test called NIFT Entrance Exam.
Top Colleges: IIT Delhi, DKTE Textile and Engineering Institute, National Institute of Fashion Technology (NIFT), Anna University, PSG College of Technology, UPTTI Kanpur
Top Recruiters: Arvind Mills, Raymond, Vardhman Textiles, Welspun India, Reliance Industries, Grasim Industries
Notable People: Sanjay Lalbhai: Chairman of Arvind Mills, major textile company | Dilip Kumar Jain: veteran textile engineering researcher in India
Sources: NIRF rankings, AmbitionBox, Glassdoor India, industry placement reports
Common Specializations (Optional): Yarn and Fabric Manufacturing: focuses on spinning fibres into yarn and weaving fabric | Textile Chemical Processing: works on dyeing, printing, and finishing fabric | Technical Textiles: designs specialised fabrics used in medical, industrial, or protective gear

A Day in the Life: A veterinarian examines sick or injured animals, gives them medicine or performs surgery, and advises pet owners or farmers on how to keep animals healthy. A typical day could involve vaccinating a farmer's cattle in the morning and treating a pet dog's broken leg in the afternoon.
Real-World Impact: Veterinarians keep India's massive dairy and livestock industry healthy, which is vital since India is the world's largest milk producer, and they also treat pets for millions of urban families through clinics and chains like Wiggles.in. Their work protects both animal welfare and the farmers who depend on healthy livestock for income.
Entry Exams: NEET (National Eligibility cum Entrance Test, the same exam used for medical college admissions) is used for admission to B.V.Sc. (Bachelor of Veterinary Science) programs in India.
Top Colleges: Indian Veterinary Research Institute (IVRI) Bareilly, Madras Veterinary College Chennai, Guru Angad Dev Veterinary and Animal Sciences University (GADVASU), Bombay Veterinary College, National Dairy Research Institute (NDRI)
Top Recruiters: State animal husbandry departments, Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR), dairy cooperatives like Amul, private pet clinics and hospitals, zoos and wildlife parks
Notable People: Dr. Ilayaraja Ramasamy (well-known wildlife veterinarian), Dr. R. V. Asokan (Indian Veterinary Association leader), Dr. Y.P. Singh (veterinary and livestock expert)
Sources: NIRF rankings, AmbitionBox, Glassdoor India, industry placement reports
Common Specializations (Optional): Livestock/Farm Animal Care: Treats cows, buffaloes, goats, and other farm animals, often working closely with farmers. | Companion Animal (Pet) Care: Treats dogs, cats, and other pets, usually in city clinics. | Wildlife Veterinary Medicine: Cares for wild animals in zoos, national parks, or rescue centres.

A Day in the Life: A zoologist studies animals and their behaviour, either out in forests and rivers observing wildlife, or in a lab analyzing animal samples and data. They might track tiger populations using camera traps, study how climate change affects birds, or write research papers on their findings.
Real-World Impact: Zoologists help protect endangered species like the Bengal tiger and the Asiatic lion through projects run by the Wildlife Institute of India, and their research guides government decisions on protecting forests and national parks like Jim Corbett and Kaziranga. Their work directly shapes how India balances development with saving its wildlife.
Entry Exams: No single fixed entrance exam for a bachelor's degree — admission is usually based on Class 12 marks in Science. For a master's or research program, exams like CUET-PG or CSIR-UGC NET (a national exam for research fellowships and lectureship eligibility) are commonly used.
Top Colleges: University of Delhi, Wildlife Institute of India (WII) Dehradun, St. Xavier's College Mumbai, Madras Christian College, University of Calcutta, Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU)
Top Recruiters: Wildlife Institute of India, Zoological Survey of India, Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, WWF-India (World Wide Fund for Nature), zoos and national parks
Where You Can Work: Tier-2 cities fine (fieldwork often in rural/forest areas)
Notable People: Salim Ali (India's most famous ornithologist, 'Birdman of India'), Ullas Karanth (tiger conservation scientist), Kartik Shanker (marine biologist and conservationist)
Sources: NIRF rankings, AmbitionBox, Glassdoor India, industry placement reports
